## Summary

Spanish-language systems account pitching its Nasdaq-100 momentum rotation: "350+ backtests to improve my Nasdaq 100 momentum system (testing, not over-optimizing 😅)". Headline stats: 37% annual since 2003 in backtest vs 9.5% for the S&P 500; max drawdown −23.6% vs −56.8%; not a single negative year in 24. The system link is deliberately not in the tweet — "Enlace en mi perfil" (link in my profile), the classic funnel pattern.

## Why it matters

- Same strategy family as Peter's NDX momentum rotation captured the same morning ([[2026-11-19-systematicpeter-vol-targeting-ndx-momentum]]) — but with the opposite transparency posture: Peter posts live positions; this account posts backtest stats and routes you to a profile link.
- Skepticism gates, in order: (1) **37% ann / 24y / zero negative years from public-index momentum would be elite-fund territory** — sustained ~27pp/yr over an index with 9.5% CAGR is the signature shape of overfitting or look-ahead (NDX membership survivorship — the index adds winners retroactively to the index's performance but a live strategy can't hold future winners), not of a free lunch. (2) "350 backtests (not over-optimizing 😅)" — the smiley is doing honest work; 350 evaluations of a rule family on one 24y sample is exactly the multiple-testing regime that manufactures great backtests. (3) The photo stats confirm consistency between claim and chart (CAGR 37.17% OCR-matches the 37%), so the numbers aren't typos — they're the claim. (4) Funnel: rules/course presumably monetized behind the profile link, uncaptured.
- The genuinely useful artifact in the pair is Peter's live-positions page — see the Inbox task comparing the two.
